newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Transport the key to Asian prosperity --financier.
newsitem.headline: Transport the key to Asian prosperity --financier.

text.p: Asia must make urban transport among its top priorities if the region is to maximise its potential as the world's most dynamic economic hub in the next century, an Asian finance expert said on Tuesday.
"Infrastructure is the basis for economic growth," said Koji Kashiwaya, a former director of the World Bank in Tokyo and now president of Singapore-based AIDEC Management Company Pte Ltd.
"Urban development including urban transport should be on top of the agenda for the next century," he told a conference on urban transport.

He warned Asia faced "a critical crisis in the shortage of infrastructure in our major cities", in the next century. Kashiwaya said the World Bank forecast there would be 27 "mega-cities" with populations of at least 10 million by 2010.
Up to 17 will be in developing countries and 12 will be in Asia, but "only one of the 12 will have a major mass rapid transport system", Kashiwaya said.

About US$2 trillion would have to be invested in Asia's infrastructure over the next 10 years to meet the explosive demand for transport services which would have to come from the private sector, Kashiwaya told Reuters after his speech.

"Infrastructure has to depend on the private sector because governments have no money," he said. "Politicians and parliament cannot solve the problem. Governments should create the framework conditions necessary to raise finance and allow the private sector to participate."
Other delegates at the conference emphasised the need for mass transport systems in major cities as a factor in economic development.

"Economic growth in big cities needs mobilisation of specialised labour," said B.I. Singhal, managing director of Rail India Technical & Economic Services Ltd, (RITES). "Traffic congestion in cities does not allow labour to move freely and affects the efficiency of a city," he said.
